A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Museum-65 dataset, fine-tuned models and five-task benchmark. The complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices support comparison despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: v1 reports original BLIP and LLaVA experiments, human-expert comparisons, training ablations, and multi-angle and multilingual evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds VLM comparisons, semantic evaluation, geographic analysis and MUZE experiments.

M1.justification: The BLIP and LoRA-fine-tuned LLaVA procedures remain unchanged, including selecting one random question per image per epoch. The expanded curation account documents the existing dataset construction rather than establishing a revised method.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual training and evaluation on the MUZE art/history benchmark, previously discussed only as related work (Appendix D.1). Museum-65 and its five tasks remain. The new language breakdown documents the existing multilingual pool rather than establishing expanded language coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds evaluated GPT-4o, Claude-3-7-sonnet, Llama-3.2-90b-vision and Gemini 1.5B flash comparators. Table 17 also introduces MUZE-trained BLIP. These substantially broaden comparisons beyond the original BLIP/LLaVA variants and human experts.

E3.justification: v2 adds METEOR and WMD-based accuracy, a separate 515-pair test-image reasoning evaluation, continent-balanced evaluation using 1,000 images per continent, and MUZE transfer comparisons. The reported human-study sample changes from 100 to 850 pairs. These are substantial protocol additions and reported revisions, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses examine geographic performance imbalance (Table 8), reasoning on training versus unseen test images (Tables 5–6), and transfer between MUZE and Museum-65 (Table 17). The original viewpoint-robustness, training-size and question-sampling analyses remain.

E5.justification: Section 5.3 adds an agreement analysis involving five experts and 63 questions, reporting 52.7% agreement against a stated 6.25% chance reference and calling this an approximation to Fleiss's kappa. Neither version reports repeated-run variability or confidence intervals for model performance.

E6.justification: v2 adds SOTA-comparison, semantic-metric, held-out reasoning, continent-wise and MUZE results. For example, Table 17 reports MUZE partial precision of 79.77 for Museum-65-trained BLIP versus 67.84 for MUZE-trained BLIP. Original general-VQA scores remain identical in v1 Table 12 and v2 Table 18. The original reasoning table's BLEU2 entries are removed.

T1.justification: Neither version develops theoretical propositions or proofs. Existing overlap-metric definitions are retained, partly relocated to Appendix C.2. The added standard metric descriptions and agreement reporting do not introduce a new theoretical framework or derivation.

C1.justification: Alongside the retained dataset, benchmark and BLIP-versus-LLaVA reasoning contributions, v2 makes domain-specific fine-tuning's necessity and superiority over current SOTA VLMs explicit headline claims in the abstract and introduction. This substantially expands the comparative scope of the central empirical claims.

C2.justification: v2 expands the original regional-imbalance and metadata-quality limitations into discussions of selection, language, framing and model-inherited biases, with an explicit academic-use boundary (Sections 3.3–3.4; Appendices B.9–B.10). It also adds interpretations concerning unseen-image generalization and the distribution of training benefits across continents.

D1.justification: v2 substantially documents curation staffing and duration, API/BeautifulSoup collection, per-museum cleaning, centralized question review and programmatic schema validation (Section 3.2; Appendix B.5). These are newly disclosed details, not demonstrated pipeline changes. Reported hardware changes from 16 to 64 H100 GPUs; core optimization hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning dataset bias, debiasing, retrieval and evaluation metrics, while removing several citations accompanying the shortened video-VQA discussion. It sharpens the MUZE scalability critique and adds empirical positioning against MUZE, while retaining the broader related-work framework.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial introductory and explanatory passages are rewritten. The former Benchmark section becomes Evaluation, task descriptions are integrated into experiment subsections, data splits move into the dataset section, and detailed metric explanations move to the appendix. The appendix structure is substantially expanded.

P2.justification: v2 adds six substantive tables covering SOTA comparisons, semantic scores, test-image reasoning, continents, language distribution and MUZE comparisons. Existing figures are largely retained but relocated; the MultiAngle table gains an explicit angle column, captions are revised, and the reasoning table loses its BLEU2 column.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens evaluation through semantic metrics and a separate unseen-image reasoning test, while making curation and bias limitations clearer. These provide a net quality gain. However, the new SOTA and MUZE comparisons lack important protocol details, and the agreement analysis does not justify its 6.25% chance reference, limiting support for the expanded superiority claims.
